classification.difficultyReason: Use the straight-line supplement and triangle angle sum to find an intermediate sloping side by the sine rule, then transfer that side into the right triangle to calculate the height.

content.prompt: Find $h$, correct to the nearest centimetre.

spec.description: P, Q and R are collinear in that order, with S vertically above R. PS, QS and RS are drawn. A separate dimension arrow spans PQ only. Ordinary source blue geometry is rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: PQ = 10 m; angle SPQ = 30 degrees; angle SQR = 72 degrees; angle QRS = 90 degrees; RS = h metres.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and the unknown h are visible.

answer.short:
$h\approx7.11\text{ m}$.

Use the sine rule to find $QS$, then $h=QS\sin72^{\circ}$.
answer.worked:
Since $P$, $Q$ and $R$ lie on a straight line:
$$\begin{align*}\angle PQS&=180^{\circ}-72^{\circ}\\\angle PQS&=108^{\circ}\\\angle PSQ&=180^{\circ}-30^{\circ}-108^{\circ}\\\angle PSQ&=42^{\circ}.\end{align*}$$
Apply the sine rule in $\triangle PQS$:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{QS}{\sin30^{\circ}}&=\frac{10}{\sin42^{\circ}}\\QS&=\frac{10\sin30^{\circ}}{\sin42^{\circ}}\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
In right-angled triangle $QRS$, keeping the intermediate value exact:
$$\begin{align*}\sin72^{\circ}&=\frac{h}{QS}\\h&=QS\sin72^{\circ}\\h&=\frac{10\sin30^{\circ}\sin72^{\circ}}{\sin42^{\circ}}\\h&\approx7.11\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
This is correct to the nearest centimetre.
